Balbieriskis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kaunas County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Balbieriškis was likely one of the earliest Jewish settlements in Lithuania, present from the 17th century as one of 246 Polish settlements with no restrictions on Jewish residents; the community numbered 1,167 by 1861, supported by two synagogues. On the eve of Yom Kippur in 1881, during a regular market day, farmers raided the town's Jewish shops in a pogrom. By the late 19th century, Balbieriškis had become an important commercial center, with trade concentrated almost entirely in Jewish hands. Following the German occupation in June 1941, local Lithuanians beat Jews and forced them into labor; Jews were marched to Prienai and murdered there on August 27, 1941, while women and children were sent to Marijampolė and killed on September 1.
